deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 63-65): Grothendieck is setting up a combinatorial model of a stratified space or stratified topos X with strata indexed by an ordered set I. For each stratum he has the open stratum X_i^*. For each 'elementary' pair i<j (j an immediate successor of i) he has a tubular neighbourhood V_ij of X_i and the deleted tubular neighbourhood V_ij^* = V_ij minus X_i, which lies inside X_j^*. On the previous page he argued that, 'in reasonable cases', the only morphisms among these 'elementary topos-pieces' are X_i^* -> V_ij, V_ij^* -> X_j^* and V_ij^* -> V_ij. This page says these are the solid arrows of the fundamental diagrams (17). He then encodes them abstractly. From the poset I he builds a diagram (a small category / quiver) I~. Its vertices are formal symbols i^* (for i in I) and [i,j], [i,j]^* (for i<j elementary). Its arrows are, for each elementary interval, the pattern (19): [i,j]^* -> [i,j] <- i^*, together with [i,j]^* -> [j]^* (here [j]^* means j^*). Counting: with nu = number of elementary intervals, I~ has card I + 2nu vertices and 3nu arrows. When I has two elements i<j, I~ is just (19). When I = Delta_r = {0<1<...<r}, substituting the geometric objects gives the zig-zag ladder (20) on the next page: X_0^* -> V_01 <- V_01^* -> X_1^* -> V_12 <- V_12^* -> X_2^* ... -> X_r^*. The next page treats the posets 'V' and 'Lambda'. The purpose is to describe the stratified object as a diagram of (unstratified) topoi or spaces indexed by I~, i.e. 'dévissage' / gluing data. Since V_ij retracts onto X_i^* (morally), each elementary piece is essentially the span X_i^* <- V_ij^* -> X_j^*, the 'link' correspondence. The page ends by moving on to an integer-valued function on I (dimension or codimension), on the next page.
errors: Notational slip: the vertex set is first described with symbols [i] (and i^*), but diagram (19) uses i^* and [j]^*; [i] and i^* are meant to be the same vertex.
'If I contains exactly two elements i<j, this diagram is (19)' is fine, but (19) was already introduced as the generic local pattern, so the labelling is slightly circular.

Mathematical gap: using only elementary intervals (covering relations) captures the full homotopy-theoretic gluing data only when non-adjacent strata do not interact. Example: a cone on a cone, where the deleted neighbourhood of X_0 also meets X_2. In general one needs links attached to all pairs i<j and to longer flags i_0<...<i_k, as in Esquisse §5 and later homotopy-link / exit-path theory. The restriction relies on the 'reasonable case' hypotheses of p.63, which are not stated precisely.
Transcription/handwriting: the objects in the last line are almost certainly V_ij^*, V_ij (as on the next page), not U_ij.

ideas.what: Describing a stratified space or topos by a diagram of open strata, tubular neighbourhoods and deleted tubular neighbourhoods (X_i^* -> V_ij <- V_ij^* -> X_j^*)
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / dévissage data of a stratified space via homotopy links (links of strata); exit-path description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom-Mather (control data), Quinn (homotopy links, 1988), MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie (exit paths), Ayala-Francis-Tanaka, Barwick-Glasman-Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'théorie de dévissage des structures stratifiées' (tubular neighbourhoods and their boundaries, diagrams of spaces indexed by flags of strata), at the level of program

ideas.what: Combinatorial indexing category I~ built from a poset I using only elementary (covering) intervals; vertex and arrow count card I + 2nu, 3nu; zig-zag ladder for I = Delta_r
ideas.modern_name: Indexing shape for a 'zig-zag' gluing diagram (cf. subdivision / twisted-arrow-type constructions on a poset)

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to encode a stratified topos by a diagram of 'elementary topos-pieces' indexed by a poset-derived shape I~ using only adjacent strata. Neither the reconstruction theorem (stratified topos <-> I~-diagram of topoi) nor the hypotheses ('cas raisonnables') under which adjacent strata suffice are carried out here. This is a topos-theoretic precursor of the stratified-homotopy-hypothesis program, but in an elementary-interval form that is weaker than the later flag/exit-path formulations.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It documents Grothendieck working concretely on the dévissage program of the Esquisse in a topos setting, but the content is subsumed by later exit-path / stratified ∞-topos work.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine combinatorial set-up (vertex and arrow counting, ladder diagrams) for the stratum / tubular-neighbourhood / link description of stratified spaces, already announced in Esquisse §5 and developed later by others. It is historically nice as a concrete working-out, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'fabriquons deux un diagramme' should read 'fabriquons donc un diagramme'.
Vertex description reads roughly: 'dont les sommets sont les i^*, des symboles [i], [i,j], [i,j]^*, où i,j ∈ I, j successeur de i'.
'qui sont toutes décrites dans' is followed by diagram (19); the marginal label '(19)' belongs to that diagram.
Last line: 'X_i^*, V_ij^*, V_ij que relient le diagramme', with V rather than U (consistent with the next page).
Insertion reads 'si ν = card de l'ens des intervalles (i<j) élémentaires, i.e. tels que j soit successeur de i'; the insertion 'i.e. I ≃ Δ_1' refers to I having exactly two elements.
